chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
When the camel has become accustomed to its load, its owner becomes liable (for any damage or loss).

key_terms.اِسْتَبْرَكَ: To become accustomed or habituated (to a load or task)
key_terms.ضَمِنَ: To be liable or responsible (for damage/loss)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on an owner's liability for their animal once it is accustomed to its load?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Ijarat* (leasing/renting) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the transfer of risk: once a camel is 'tested' or accustomed (*istabarak*) to a load, the owner guarantees its fitness for that specific burden. This principle underscores the owner's liability for latent defects or failure to perform, ensuring fairness in commercial transactions by holding the proprietor accountable for the animal's established capacity.
